liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes of the World** (5 reviews): Weir's guitar was spectacularly out of tune at the start of the song; Agrees Weir's guitar was badly off during Eyes; reviewer attended the show and had this tape [23][24][28][29][34]
- **Revolutionary Hamstrung Blues** (2 reviews, 2 other sources): Mydland and Lesh performed this duet only at this show; the reviewer wonders why it was dropped; Only known performance; after the show, tapers puzzled over what it was, and the soundboard makes more words audible [1][6][23][26]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer says the band took the first set to another level with Minglewood [29]
- **Supplication Jam** (1 review): Band tried a smooth transition from Supplication into Promised Land, but it doesn't quite work [26]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 other source): A Black Peter tease comes before Wharf Rat [12]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer thinks Sugar Magnolia raised the intensity after the Eyes trouble [28]
- Called a very solid opener, flowing into Peggy-O [26]

## Setlist highlights

- **Revolutionary Hamstrung Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [35]
- **Black Peter tease**: back after 146 archived shows (720 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [35]
- **Bob talk**: rare: 3 archived performances [35]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-03-27.beyerm88.pinney.russjcan.107068.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 140 min [1]
- **gd1986-03-27.167372.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 142 min [6]
- **gd1986-03-27.177015.RealisticPressureZone.Chamberlain.Chamberlain.flac2448**: source not stated; 20 songs; 144 min [11]
- **gd1986-03-27.156131.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 20 songs; 143 min [12]
- **gd86-03-27.sbd.miller.26347.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 138 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [16]. Said about its sound: Second-set soundboard quality is only OK, possibly due to patches [31]
- **gd86-03-27.neumann-hogan.fixed.24029.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 136 min; rated 4.17/5 by 18 [19]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls it a great-sounding audience recording; Neumann U87 mics shine: full, rich, sweet low end and surprising dynamic range for a cassette audience master; Tape still sounds great to the reviewer, who suggests the venue's acoustics were excellent [23][27][28][34]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was at the show and says they were extremely high, possibly explaining why they missed the guitar problem [24]
- General admission crowd with a good vibe; it had rained during the day, and people enjoyed Bertha [29]
- Local attendee recalls a bad high, hostile-looking sweaty faces on the floor, and unconscious patrons near the rafters in the second set [33]
- Reviewer felt they were witnessing the start of the band's decline [33]
- Civic Center had warm sound; attendee says you could feel the floor and touch the ice [34]
- Encore was Day Job [1]
- Show began before the taper was ready, clipping the head of Jack Straw [11]
- Before Hamstrung Blues, Weir quipped about it taking a heap of homing to make a pigeon toed, nodding to Walt Kelly's Pogo [12]
- First set is nice through Supplication Jam, but afterward the band seems rushed and falls apart [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-03-27.beyerm88.pinney.russjcan.107068.flac16**: taped by Tom Pinney; transferred by Russ Cansler; source: Beyer M-88's XY 90w/D5 40 feet away,5 feet high,center [1]
- **gd1986-03-27.167372.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [6]
- **gd1986-03-27.177015.RealisticPressureZone.Chamberlain.Chamberlain.flac2448**: taped by Richard Chamberlain; transferred by Win Chamberlain; source: Microphones/Realistic Pressure Zone. Each was mounted on a 1ft square sheet of 1/8 inch plexiglass. Auto leveling used. [11]. Also: Taper recorded each set on one tape using tracks 1-4, rewinding between sets; a crease near 8 minutes affected every track; Realistic pressure zone mics were placed about 40 feet behind the soundboard, nearly dead center [11]
- **gd1986-03-27.156131.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew; Mike Davis, Kenny Davis, Sean Murtha, Kyle Holbrook, Tom Pinney, Gary Steel, Greg Martens; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: speed corrected 1.75% Microphones: set 1 Beyer m201 (hypercardioid) XY 90º set 2 AKG 422 XY fig 8's > Nakamichi 550 > Recorder: Sony TC-D5M No Dolby Maxell… [12]. Also: Missed start was filled with 3:24 borrowed from the Pinney Beyerm88 first-generation source [12]
- **gd86-03-27.sbd.miller.26347.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Cassette Master> Reel> Dat> ?> Dat> CD -> EAC> SHN with aud patches by Charlie Miller [16]
- **gd86-03-27.neumann-hogan.fixed.24029.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB(CENTER)>AUD>MC>CDR Neumann U87's>Uher CR240>Maxell XLII 90 Cass. Master>Marantz Pro CDR 500 Paul Hogan recording. Note: Original seed (shnid#5003) was TAO.… [19]

claims.text: Mydland and Lesh performed this duet only at this show; the reviewer wonders why it was dropped
Weir's guitar was spectacularly out of tune at the start of the song
Reviewer calls it a great-sounding audience recording
Agrees Weir's guitar was badly off during Eyes; reviewer attended the show and had this tape
Reviewer was at the show and says they were extremely high, possibly explaining why they missed the guitar problem
Called a very solid opener, flowing into Peggy-O
Only known performance; after the show, tapers puzzled over what it was, and the soundboard makes more words audible
Band tried a smooth transition from Supplication into Promised Land, but it doesn't quite work
Neumann U87 mics shine: full, rich, sweet low end and surprising dynamic range for a cassette audience master
Reviewer suspects Weir broke a string before Eyes, causing trouble, but the band recovered with a strong improvisation
Reviewer thinks Sugar Magnolia raised the intensity after the Eyes trouble
Tape still sounds great to the reviewer, who suggests the venue's acoustics were excellent
General admission crowd with a good vibe; it had rained during the day, and people enjoyed Bertha
Reviewer, second from the rail before Jerry, says Garcia seemed to be easing out of the ending, ready to leave
Reviewer says the band took the first set to another level with Minglewood
First set is nice through Supplication Jam, but afterward the band seems rushed and falls apart
Second-set soundboard quality is only OK, possibly due to patches
Local attendee recalls a bad high, hostile-looking sweaty faces on the floor, and unconscious patrons near the rafters in the second set
Reviewer felt they were witnessing the start of the band's decline
Civic Center had warm sound; attendee says you could feel the floor and touch the ice
Weir's out-of-tune guitar was as painful then as on the tape
Audience recording captures the hall's warm sound well; reviewer rates sound great
Uploader says this was the only time the band ever played it
Encore was Day Job
Master cassettes came from Doug Lamarre; Charlie Miller did the transfer and coordinated the effort
Only performance of the song
Taper recorded each set on one tape using tracks 1-4, rewinding between sets; a crease near 8 minutes affected every track
Realistic pressure zone mics were placed about 40 feet behind the soundboard, nearly dead center
Show began before the taper was ready, clipping the head of Jack Straw
Missed start was filled with 3:24 borrowed from the Pinney Beyerm88 first-generation source
Before Hamstrung Blues, Weir quipped about it taking a heap of homing to make a pigeon toed, nodding to Walt Kelly's Pogo
A Black Peter tease comes before Wharf Rat
